About Maine FFA

The Maine FFA Association, with a picture of award winners  (formerly known as "Future Farmers of America"), subscribes to the mission of the National FFA Organization: 

"FFA makes a positive difference in the lives of students by developing their potential for premier leadership, personal growth and career success through agricultural education." Maine FFA has 417 members, with chapters located throughout the state. The association is led by a team of student officers.

 

 

Membership & Joining

As part of the overall effort in Maine Agriculture & Natural Resources Education, middle and high school students eligible for FFA membership are those enrolled in at least one course related to agriculture (including aquaculture, agriscience, biotechnology, forestry, horticulture, natural resource management, and other biological and physical science courses that include applications to agriculture). 

Those wishing to start a new FFA chapter should contact Emily Doughty, Maine FFA State Liaison. The Maine FFA Constitution and Bylaws are available for additional information on chartering a chapter.  The Maine FFA Guidebook is an additional resource for new and existing chapters.  

 

Get Involved

FFA Opportunities

Opportunities within FFA include:

  • Competitive agriculture/natural resource events at local, state, and national levels
  • Student workshops and leadership events
  • Eligibility for numerous national-level achievement awards and scholarships
  • Public speaking events
  • Advanced independent projects ("supervised agricultural experiences")
  • International and U.S. travel opportunities
  • Community development activities

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 1 address is shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — Emily.Doughty@Maine.gov → Emily.Doughty@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Let very uneven cards find their own height
decisions.why: 1 row pairs a short card with one holding nearly three times as much. Equal heights stretch the short one and the difference reads as a hole, so these are allowed to sit at the height of what is in them.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.

decisions.label: Size an image by its shape
decisions.why: "FFA Photo" measures 2048×1536 — it was sitting in the flow at its own pixel size, aligned with nothing.

decisions.label: Let a bold line dividing a card be its heading
decisions.why: 2 lines inside the cards are a paragraph holding nothing but a few bold words — "August 2026" is one — with the part of the card it names underneath. That is a heading, and set as a paragraph it carries no level, so the card offers nothing to scan by and a screen reader announces only running text. Each becomes an h3 and takes the same section bar the other card headings use. Only where a card has two or more, which is what makes them divisions rather than one stressed line. Not a word changes.

decisions.label: Add a contents list (4 sections)
decisions.why: Built from the section headings already on the page. Below three sections a list is not a route.
